KW:abstract.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}abstract{/c} keyword marks a class or member as incomplete, requiring a concrete implementation to be provided in a derived class.

KW:add.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}add{/c} keyword defines how a handler is attached to an event. It runs when code subscribes to the event.

KW:alias.Definition: {c:color-blue keyword}alias{/c} creates an alternate name for a namespace or type to help simplify long or conflicting qualified names.

KW:and.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}and{/c} keyword combines two patterns in a pattern matching expression, requiring both to match.

KW:ascending.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}ascending{/c} keyword sorts query results from lowest to highest.

KW:async.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}async{/c} keyword marks a method or lambda expression as asynchronous, allowing it to suspend execution at {c:color-purple keyword}await{/c} points while waiting for operations to complete.

KW:await.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}await{/c} keyword pauses execution of the enclosing asynchronous method or lambda expression until the awaited expression completes.

KW:base.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}base{/c} keyword refers to the parent class of the current class, giving access to its members.

KW:bool.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}bool{/c} keyword declares a Boolean type that represents either {c:bold}true{/c} or {c:bold}false{/c}.

KW:by.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}by{/c} keyword specifies how data should be grouped or ordered in a query expression.

KW:byte.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}byte{/c} keyword declares an 8-bit unsigned integer type that stores whole numbers from 0 to 255.

KW:break.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}break{/c} keyword immediately exits the current loop or switch statement.

KW:case:ControlFlow.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}case{/c} keyword labels a specific match in a {c:color-purple keyword}switch{/c} statement, identifying the value that causes this branch to execute.

KW:case:PatternMatching.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}case{/c} keyword labels a pattern branch in a {c:color-purple keyword}switch{/c} statement, identifying the pattern that causes this branch to execute.

KW:catch.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}catch{/c} keyword marks the block that runs when an exception is thrown in the preceding {c:color-purple keyword}try{/c} block.

KW:char.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}char{/c} keyword declares a type that holds a single Unicode character.

KW:checked.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}checked{/c} keyword enables overflow checking for numeric operations. It causes an error if a calculation exceeds the allowed range.

KW:class.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}class{/c} keyword introduces a class declaration, which is a reference type blueprint for creating objects.

KW:const.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}const{/c} keyword declares a value that is fixed at compile time and cannot be changed.

KW:continue.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}continue{/c} keyword skips the remaining code in the current loop iteration and immediately starts the next one.

KW:decimal.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}decimal{/c} keyword declares a high-precision 128-bit numeric type commonly used for financial and monetary calculations.

KW:default:Literal.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}default{/c} keyword represents the default value for the specified type — zero for value types and {c:color-blue keyword}null{/c} for reference types.

KW:default.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}default{/c} label provides a fallback branch in a switch statement when no other case matches.

KW:delegate.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}delegate{/c} keyword introduces a delegate type declaration, which is a type that stores a reference to a method with a matching signature.

KW:descending.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}descending{/c} keyword sorts query results from highest to lowest.

KW:do.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}do{/c} keyword starts a loop that always executes at least once before its condition is checked.

KW:double.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}double{/c} keyword declares a 64-bit double-precision floating-point type.

KW:dynamic.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}dynamic{/c} keyword defers type checking until runtime. It allows flexible behavior but removes compile-time type safety.

KW:else.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}else{/c} keyword marks a block that executes when the preceding {c:color-purple keyword}if{/c} condition is false.

KW:enum.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}enum{/c} keyword introduces an enum declaration, which defines a named set of constant integer values.

KW:equals.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}equals{/c} keyword specifies the matching condition in a {c:color-blue keyword}join{/c} clause, comparing values from two data sources.

KW:event.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}event{/c} keyword introduces an event declaration, defining a notification mechanism that other code can subscribe to.

KW:explicit.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}explicit{/c} keyword defines a user-defined type conversion that requires an explicit cast in order to be applied.

KW:extern.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}extern{/c} keyword indicates that a member is implemented outside of C# code, typically in native or runtime-provided code.

KW:false.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}false{/c} keyword is a Boolean literal representing the value false.

KW:file.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}file{/c} keyword is an access modifier that limits the visibility of a type declaration to the file in which it is defined.

KW:finally.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}finally{/c} keyword marks a block that always executes after the {c:color-purple keyword}try{/c} block, regardless of whether an exception was thrown.

KW:fixed.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}fixed{/c} keyword pins a managed variable in memory, preventing the garbage collector from moving it.

KW:float.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}float{/c} keyword declares a 32-bit single-precision floating-point type with less precision than {c:color-blue keyword}double{/c}.

KW:for.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}for{/c} keyword introduces a loop controlled by an initializer, a condition, and an iterator expression.

KW:foreach.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}foreach{/c} keyword starts a loop that iterates over each element in a collection or sequence one at a time.

KW:from.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}from{/c} keyword introduces a query expression and specifies the data source to query.

KW:get.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}get{/c} keyword defines how a property's value is retrieved. It runs when the property is read.

KW:global.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}global{/c} keyword refers to the global namespace, allowing types to be accessed without any namespace qualification.

KW:group.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}group{/c} keyword groups query results into sequences based on a specified key.

KW:goto.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}goto{/c} keyword transfers execution unconditionally to a labeled statement elsewhere in the code.

KW:if.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}if{/c} keyword introduces a conditional branch that executes only when its condition evaluates to {c:bold}true{/c}.

KW:implicit.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}implicit{/c} keyword defines a user-defined type conversion that is applied automatically without requiring an explicit cast.

KW:in:ArgumentModifier.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}in{/c} argument modifier passes the argument by reference as {c:bold}read-only{/c}, ensuring it cannot be modified by the called method.

KW:in:LoopStatement.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}in{/c} keyword separates the loop variable from the collection being iterated in a {c:color-purple keyword}foreach{/c} statement.

KW:in:ParameterModifier.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}in{/c} parameter modifier declares that this parameter is passed by reference but is {c:bold}read-only{/c} — the method cannot modify the caller's original value.

KW:in:QueryExpression.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}in{/c} keyword in a query expression specifies the data source that the preceding range variable iterates over.

KW:init.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}init{/c} keyword defines a property accessor that can only be called during object initialization, making the property read-only afterward.

KW:int.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}int{/c} keyword declares a 32-bit signed integer type that stores whole numbers from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647.

KW:interface.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}interface{/c} keyword introduces an interface declaration, defining a contract of members that any implementing type must provide.

KW:internal.Definition: {c:color-blue keyword}internal{/c} members are accessible from any code within the same assembly but not from other assemblies.

KW:into.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}into{/c} keyword introduces a continuation variable that captures the results of a preceding {c:color-blue keyword}group{/c} or {c:color-blue keyword}join{/c} clause for further querying.

KW:join.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}join{/c} keyword combines elements from two data sources based on a matching condition.

KW:let.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}let{/c} keyword introduces a new range variable in a query expression that stores the result of an expression for reuse later in the query.

KW:lock.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}lock{/c} keyword acquires an exclusive lock on a specified object, ensuring only one thread can enter the associated block at a time.

KW:long.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}long{/c} keyword declares a 64-bit signed integer type for storing very large whole numbers.

KW:managed.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}managed{/c} keyword specifies that a function pointer uses a managed calling convention.

KW:namespace.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}namespace{/c} keyword declares a scope that contains related type declarations and helps organize code into logical groups.

KW:new:ObjectConstruction.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}new{/c} keyword creates a new instance of a type. It allocates memory and initializes the object.

KW:new:MemberModifier.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}new{/c} member modifier hides a member inherited from a base class with a new declaration, intentionally breaking the inheritance link.

KW:nint.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}nint{/c} keyword declares a native-sized signed integer whose bit width matches the target platform (32-bit or 64-bit).

KW:not.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}not{/c} keyword negates a pattern in a pattern matching expression, matching any value that does not satisfy the pattern.

KW:notnull.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}notnull{/c} keyword is a generic type constraint that restricts the type argument to non-nullable types.

KW:nuint.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}nuint{/c} keyword declares a native-sized unsigned integer whose bit width matches the target platform (32-bit or 64-bit).

KW:null.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}null{/c} keyword represents the absence of an object reference or nullable value.

KW:object.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}object{/c} keyword declares the universal base type from which all other C# types ultimately derive.

KW:on.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}on{/c} keyword specifies the equality condition for matching elements in a {c:color-blue keyword}join{/c} clause.

KW:operator.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}operator{/c} keyword introduces an operator overload declaration, defining custom behavior for a built-in operator symbol.

KW:or.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}or{/c} keyword combines two patterns in a pattern matching expression, matching if either pattern applies.

KW:orderby.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}orderby{/c} keyword sorts query results by one or more keys in ascending or descending order.

KW:out.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}out{/c} modifier designates a variable as an output — the method must assign a value to it before returning, and at the call site it does not need to be initialized before being passed.

KW:override.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}override{/c} keyword provides a new implementation for a virtual or abstract member inherited from a base class.

KW:params.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}params{/c} keyword marks a parameter as accepting a variable number of arguments, which are collected into an array.

KW:partial.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}partial{/c} keyword allows a type or method declaration to be split across multiple files, with each part marked with {c:color-blue keyword}partial{/c}.

KW:private.Definition: {c:color-blue keyword}private{/c} members are only accessible within the class or struct in which they are declared.

KW:protected.Definition: {c:color-blue keyword}protected{/c} members are accessible within the containing class and by derived (child) classes.

KW:public.Definition: {c:color-blue keyword}public{/c} members are accessible from any other code within the same assembly or another assembly that references it.

KW:readonly.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}readonly{/c} keyword marks a field so that it can only be assigned during declaration or inside a constructor.

KW:record.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}record{/c} keyword introduces a record declaration, which is a reference type with built-in value-based equality and support for non-destructive mutation.

KW:ref:LocalModifier.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}ref{/c} keyword passes a variable by reference, allowing the called code to read and modify the original variable directly.

KW:remove.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}remove{/c} keyword defines how a handler is detached from an event. It runs when code unsubscribes from the event.

KW:required.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}required{/c} keyword marks a member as mandatory to set during object initialization, causing a compile-time error if it is omitted.

KW:return.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}return{/c} keyword exits the current method and optionally passes a value back to the caller.

KW:sbyte.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}sbyte{/c} keyword declares an 8-bit signed integer type that stores whole numbers from -128 to 127.

KW:sealed.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}sealed{/c} keyword prevents a class from being used as a base class, or prevents a virtual member from being overridden in further derived classes.

KW:select.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}select{/c} keyword specifies which values are returned from a query and defines the shape of the result.

KW:set.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}set{/c} keyword defines how a property's value is assigned. It runs when a value is written to the property.

KW:short.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}short{/c} keyword declares a 16-bit signed integer type that stores whole numbers from -32,768 to 32,767.

KW:stackalloc.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}stackalloc{/c} keyword allocates a block of memory on the stack, which is automatically freed when the current scope ends.

KW:static:MemberModifier.Definition: {c:color-blue keyword}static{/c} marks a member as belonging to the type itself rather than to any instance. It can be accessed directly on the type without creating an object.

KW:static:TypeModifier.Definition: {c:color-blue keyword}static{/c} marks a type as non-instantiable and restricts it to containing only {c:color-blue keyword}static{/c} members.

KW:static:UsingDirectiveModifier.Definition: Imports the {c:color-blue keyword}static{/c} members of a type into the current scope so they can be referenced without the type name prefix.

KW:string.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}string{/c} keyword declares a type for storing an immutable sequence of Unicode characters.

KW:struct.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}struct{/c} keyword introduces a struct declaration, which is a value type that stores its data directly rather than by reference.

KW:switch.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}switch{/c} keyword introduces a switch statement or expression that evaluates a value or pattern and branches to the matching case.

KW:this.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}this{/c} keyword refers to the current object instance from within its own class or struct definition.

KW:throw.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}throw{/c} keyword raises an exception, halting normal execution and transferring control to the nearest matching {c:color-purple keyword}catch{/c} block.

KW:true.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}true{/c} keyword is a Boolean literal representing the value true.

KW:try.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}try{/c} keyword marks a block of code to be monitored for exceptions.

KW:uint.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}uint{/c} keyword declares a 32-bit unsigned integer type that stores whole numbers from 0 to 4,294,967,295.

KW:ulong.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}ulong{/c} keyword declares a 64-bit unsigned integer type for storing very large positive whole numbers.

KW:unmanaged.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}unmanaged{/c} keyword is a generic type constraint that restricts the type argument to unmanaged types — types that contain no managed references.

KW:ushort.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}ushort{/c} keyword declares a 16-bit unsigned integer type that stores whole numbers from 0 to 65,535.

KW:unchecked.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}unchecked{/c} keyword disables overflow checking for numeric operations, allowing calculations to wrap around without throwing an error.

KW:unsafe.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}unsafe{/c} keyword marks a block or member as containing code that uses pointers and other memory-unsafe operations.

KW:using:CompilationScope.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}using{/c} keyword imports a namespace into the current file, making its types available without full qualification.

KW:using:ResourceManagement.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}using{/c} keyword marks a statement that creates or uses a disposable resource and automatically disposes it when the statement or scope ends.

KW:value.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}value{/c} keyword represents the value being assigned to a property or indexer. It is implicitly provided by C# whenever the {c:color-blue keyword}set{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}init{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}add{/c}, or {c:color-blue keyword}remove{/c} accessors are invoked.

KW:var.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}var{/c} keyword lets the compiler infer the type of a variable from its assigned value. The variable still has a strong, fixed type.

KW:var:PatternMatching.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}var{/c} keyword in a pattern matches any value and introduces a binding variable for that value or a component of it.

KW:virtual.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}virtual{/c} keyword marks a member as overridable, allowing a derived class to provide its own implementation.

KW:void.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}void{/c} keyword as a return type indicates that the method does not return a value.

KW:volatile.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}volatile{/c} keyword marks a field so that reads and writes are always performed directly against main memory, without processor-level caching.

KW:when.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}when{/c} keyword adds an additional condition to a {c:color-purple keyword}catch{/c} block or {c:color-purple keyword}case{/c} label that must be true for the block to handle the exception or match.

KW:where:Constraint.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}where{/c} keyword in a generic declaration introduces a type constraint, restricting which types are valid for the type parameter.

KW:where:QueryExpression.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}where{/c} keyword in a query expression filters data based on the provided condition.

KW:while.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}while{/c} keyword starts a loop that checks its condition before each iteration and continues executing as long as the condition is {c:bold}true{/c}.

KW:with.Definition: The {c:color-blue keyword}with{/c} keyword creates a new object by copying an existing instance and applying specified member changes. This non-destructive instantiation leaves the original object unchanged.

KW:yield.Definition: The {c:color-purple keyword}yield{/c} keyword returns the next value in an iterator sequence or signals the end of the sequence.
